title: Etale splitting of a finite algebra at a geometric point
statement: Let $A$ and $C$ be commutative rings, $C$ a finite $A$-module algebra, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $\phi:A\to\Omega$ a ring map. Write $I$ for the finite set of ring maps $t:C\to\Omega$ extending $\phi$. There exist an etale $A$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a map $\phi_B:B\to\Omega$ extending $\phi$, and complete orthogonal idempotents $e_t$ in $B\otimes_A C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], indexed by $t\in I$, whose sum is one and whose values under $b\otimes c\mapsto\phi_B(b)t'(c)$ are $1$ if $t'=t$ and $0$ otherwise. This allows $I$ empty.

proof.text: The source proof first isolates one geometric point. Enlarge the base residue field by its finite separable subextension using an etale residue-field realization; the remaining residue extension is purely inseparable. Apply Mathlib 00UJ to isolate its kernel. Pure inseparability ensures that a point with this kernel is unique. Induct over the finite set of points: transport earlier idempotents through each etale base change and multiply the new one by the complements of the earlier ones. They stay orthogonal and retain their indicator values. The complementary idempotent vanishes at every point of the fibre. Its support has closed image under the finite map and misses the chosen point; invert a base element nonzero at that point to kill the complement. The resulting idempotents sum to one. This is the complete existing Lean proof in FiniteSplitting.lean:85-472; the pinned sorry map records no reachable holes.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_etale_completeOrthogonalIdempotents_forall_tensor_eq [Module.Finite A B]
    (φ : A →+* Ω) [Fintype (PointsOver φ B)] [DecidableEq (PointsOver φ B)] :
    ∃ (A' : Type u) (_ : CommRing A') (_ : Algebra A A') (_ : Algebra.Etale A A')
      (φ' : A' →+* Ω) (hφ' : φ'.comp (algebraMap A A') = φ) (e : PointsOver φ B → A' ⊗[A] B),
      CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents e ∧
        ∀ t t' : PointsOver φ B, t'.tensor hφ' (e t) = if t' = t then 1 else 0
